newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan easing immigration to woo foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan easing immigration to woo foreign investors.

text.p: Taiwan has proposed a draft law allowing foreigners to obtain permanent residency without having to give up their foreign nationality, a senior official said on Tuesday.

The residency reform aims to remove some of the bureaucratic obstacles that long have frustrated foreign investors' attempts to live and work in Taiwan, an interior ministry spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
The government has launched an ambitious effort to turn Taiwan into an Asia-Pacific financial and business hub and to lure higher levels of foreign investment.

"Under the draft immigration law, which we approved on Monday, foreigners who have lived here legally for seven years consecutively are eligible to apply for permanent residency," the ministry spokesman said.
Under current law, a foreigner must give up his original nationality before being given permanent status.
The draft still needs parliamentary approval.

Under the draft, foreigners whose spouses or parents are citizens of the exiled Republic of China on Taiwan also could be granted permanent residency after living on the island for five years consecutively, the official said.

At present, foreigners with work permits are allowed to live in Taiwan continuously, but they must leave the island -- even if only for a short while -- if their stay reaches three years, the official said.
